what: the ten code tasks with one more reader per listed answer of the flagged phrases (experiments/variant_demo.py); a cell is one model's code on one requirement, and the cells, the violations and what FCP certified before are those of results/code_<task>.json
rule: a requirement on which a new reader differs from one of the two readers, in context (a relation other than EQUIVALENT, ONLY-A, ONLY-B), is held: none of its cells is certified
lost: the cells that were certified and are not once the requirements are held: false ones (the code violates the requirement), true ones, and of the true ones those held only by comparisons that did not end (UNKNOWN), where no difference of the readings was shown

flagged.phrase: a load that would take it over
refund the charge ... and release the stock
if the customer was charged ... if it was reserved

under: a comparison compares contracts, so a new reader that assumes more than a stored reader differs from it on every requirement, on runs about which its own rules say nothing; such a pair (A-WEAKER on <assumptions>) is compared again on the runs that meet the new reader's assumptions (variant_demo.py under, tasks whose code calls a service), and totals_under counts with those comparisons in place of the first ones
rejects: a second rule, written after the results of the first were seen: a certificate says that the code meets a requirement as the two readers state it, and it stands under a new reading that accepts every run they accept; a requirement is held only where a new reader may reject a run that one of the two accepts, in context (A-WEAKER, INCOMPARABLE, UNKNOWN, NO-CONTEXT, and not A-STRONGER), and totals_rejects counts with it; held_under of a reader is the same set taken from the comparisons on the runs that meet its assumptions, where those were made
waits: the second rule as fcp review applies it (fcp.review.waiting): the comparison in context assumes the other rules of both readings and says nothing of a run on which another rule of the new reading fails, so a requirement on which a new reader differs from one of the two is let go only where no run that one of the two accepts and the new reader rejects was found in context and none without context (the relation without context is EQUIVALENT or A-STRONGER); totals_waits counts with it

apart.what: requirements on which the two readers agree with each other while a comparison with the reference reading does not show agreement, in the tasks whose readers are all compared (for a task whose code calls a service the reference is compared on the runs that meet the reader's assumptions, results/code_<task>_env.json); both: each of the two is shown to differ from the reference; one: one of them is; undecided: neither is, and a comparison did not end; accepts: a run is shown that each of the two accepts and the reference rejects, so that a certificate can be false; held: those on which a new reader differs from one of the two; held_rejects: those on which a new reader may reject a run that one of the two accepts; held_waits: those that wait under the rule of fcp review (waits)
